summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the Islamic rulings on prayer times, specifically addressing the three times when optional prayers are prohibited: sunrise, sunset, and midday. He clarifies that these prohibitions do not apply to obligatory prayers, particularly when someone has missed a prayer due to sleep or forgetfulness. Sh. Ali Mashhour emphasizes that a person who has missed an obligatory prayer must make it up immediately upon remembering, regardless of the time of day. He then introduces a hadith from the companion Absah, explaining the Prophet's prohibition against praying during sunrise and sunset, relating it to the pre-Islamic practice of sun worship in Jahiliyyah. The reasoning behind this prohibition is to avoid any outward appearance of resemblance to sun worshippers, even though the Muslim's intention differs.
suggested_title: The Times Prayer is Prohibited and the Importance of Making Up Missed Obligatory Prayers
